thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH - QuasarTech (dedicated pool qt-west-2) node gpu-118 firmware panic & repeated kernel oops — 75% of tenant requests failed, automatic drain triggered at 12:08:10 UTC. Page: @sara.

sara - oncall: acked. jumping in. any immediate customer impact notes?

pagerduty: Alert details -> service: dedpool-qt-west-2, symptom: model-serving 500s + grpc disconnects, start: 2026-02-12T12:07:58Z, affected nodes: gpu-118, gpu-119 (secondary flapping).

jamal - eng-sre: I see bulk of errors are KV cache misses + backend gRPC timeouts. gpu-118 shows repeated firmware panic stack traces in node-exporter logs: `gpu: tdr_recovery(); panic_count=4`

priya - eng-runtime: confirmed. runtime kicked an evacuation at 12:09 and started migrating active sessions. Some sessions were dropped because model state couldn't be checkpointed fast enough.

arnold - cs: customer (QuasarTech) on call. they report increased latencies and several failed inference requests for critical user flows. They asked for ETA on failover.

jamal - eng-sre: immediate plan: 1) isolate tenant routing so QuasarTech traffic is routed away from qt-west-2 dedicated pool to qt-fallback-east-1 (already compatible model variants) 2) mark gpu-118/119 quarantined 3) engage hardware team for physical replacement 4) communicate ETA to customer (Arnold).

sara - oncall: Priya — can you flip routing? Is there a simple policy change we can push to avoid breaking sessions mid-request?

priya - eng-runtime: yes. pushing a routing rule now: `route: if tenant==quasartech && pool==qt-west-2 -> qt-fallback-east-1 fallback_mode=graceful max_inflight=2`

priya - eng-runtime: pushed. note: graceful fallback will allow existing short-lived sessions to finish up to 5s; new requests will start on fallback. Adding a temporary throttle to protect fallback pool.

jamal - eng-sre: adding KV cache clear for migrating sessions to avoid stale state causing double-counting. Command: ```
# evict tenant KV cache
redwoodctl cache evict --tenant quasartech --scope=prefix
```

infra-bot: quarantine initiated for nodes [gpu-118,gpu-119]. Node states -> quarantined. Autoscaler prevented new allocations.

arnold - cs: relaying to QuasarTech: we've routed traffic to a fallback pool in a different region; there may be a ~100-200ms RTT increase for some calls. They requested an ETA for node replacement/recovery.

jamal - eng-sre: ETA for hardware swap . depends on spare availability. Opening a hardware ticket with ops: HWT-5902. If we can't hot-swap within 2 hours, we'll request an emergency reserved capacity bump for the tenant.

priya - eng-runtime: telemetry shows error rate dropping from 40% -> 8% since routing change. Throughput on fallback pool at ~60% of headroom. Throttle is protecting tail latency.

sara - oncall: good. @arnold please let QuasarTech know temporary perf impact but stable correctness. Also ask if they want a strictly regional failover (we can schedule a data-transfer assisted warm cache) or leave fallback.

arnold - cs: they prefer to stay on fallback for now but want a warm restore to west when hardware is replaced. They also want a ticket & postmortem.

jamal - eng-sre: noted. I'll keep node logs and collect firmware panic dumps. Quick paste of relevant kernel oops: ```
[  312.123456] NVRM: GPU panic: firmware exception at 0xdeadbeef
[  312.123460] RIP: 0x0000ffffdeadbeef cpu: 1 pid: 0 Comm: kernel
```

priya - eng-runtime: check: is the model variant compatible across regions? We had to fallback to a quantized v2 model; quality check shows minor probability shift (<0.6% on eval prompt set). Arnold, FYI for customer.

arnold - cs: copying to QuasarTech. they asked if we can pin responses to the previous variant — they want to avoid any distribution shift.

jamal - eng-sre: two options: 1) warm restore on new hardware in west then migrate with cache warmup and traffic mirroring 2) keep on fallback and run continuous A/B with traffic mirroring to evaluate quality. Option 1 requires a fast hardware replacement.

sara - oncall: @natalie, can platform expedite spare allocation or cross-pool move to keep them in-region?

natalie - platform-eng: checking spare inventory. we have 1 spare in us-west but cross-tenant allocation requires approval. If QuasarTech agrees to a brief maintenance window, we can do a live migrate: cordon failing nodes, boot spare as replacement, attach to dedicated pool, then migrate sessions. This will cause a ~2-3 minute maintenance for warm cache.

arnold - cs: QuasarTech prefers in-region restore if it can be done within 4 hours. They approve maintenance window.

jamal - eng-sre: plan then: 1) keep routing to fallback (already done) 2) start hardware swap prep, ticket HWT-5902 assigned to ops 3) prepare warm-restore playbook and mirroring 4) once spare is booted, test with canary traffic (5% traffic mirrored) then switch back with gradual rollout and monitoring.

priya - eng-runtime: I'll prepare the mirroring hook and gating metrics (per-token latency, perplexity on eval set, error rate). Config snippet: ```
mirror:
  source: qt-fallback-east-1
  target: qt-west-2-new
  sample_rate: 0.05
  metrics: [latency_95, error_rate, model_score_delta]
```

sara - oncall: jamal — please keep logs and timeline; we'll need this for postmortem. Also add a customer-facing incident note template and share with Arnold.

jamal - eng-sre: Will do. Capturing timeline: 12:07:58 - first panic; 12:08:10 - auto-evict; 12:09:30 - routing rule pushed; 12:12:00 - quarantine enforced; 12:20:00 - fallback capacity stable.

infra-bot: ops update -> spare gpu available in us-west, awaiting authorization to attach to qt-west-2 pool.

natalie - platform-eng: approved. Ops, proceed with hot-attach.

ops (via infra-bot): hot-attach initiated. attaching spare id: spare-43 to pool qt-west-2. expected boot ~8 minutes.

priya - eng-runtime: preparing mirroring hooks; will start sample mirroring as soon as target is healthy.

arnold - cs: relayed to QuasarTech that spare is being attached; they want to be notified before final cutover.

jamal - eng-sre: collecting panic dumps to upload to ticket. One more observation: gpu-119 had repeated ECC errors prior to panic, might be linked to firmware regression. We'll include FW version in postmortem.

ops (infra-bot): spare-43 attached, node reported healthy at 12:42:11. boot logs clean.

priya - eng-runtime: starting canary mirror at sample_rate=0.05 now. watching metrics.

priya - eng-runtime: mirror metrics: latency_95 delta ~ +20ms (within SLO), error_rate mirrored 0.2% higher, model_score_delta negligible. canary looks healthy.

jamal - eng-sre: good. scheduling gradual traffic rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over next 30 minutes, halt on error spikes.

sara - oncall: @liz I'll hand off after rollout passes. Liz, you'll own final cutover and customer communication once we hit 100%.

liz - oncall-next: ack. I'll be ready to take over. Please leave a short summary for handoff.

arnold - cs: QuasarTech acknowledged the plan and will schedule a brief maintenance notification to their users aligning with our final cutover window.

priya - eng-runtime: at 60% rollout now; metrics steady. latency within 95th SLO, error_rate trending down.

jamal - eng-sre: confirming with ops to decommission quarantined nodes once customers are fully migrated and replacement validated. We'll keep them offline for forensic analysis.

infra-bot: quarantine nodes (gpu-118,gpu-119) marked for RMA and forensic hold.

jamal - eng-sre: adding preliminary cause: likely firmware crash triggered by ECC anomaly; further root cause after firmware vendor analysis.

sara - oncall: handing off -> final notes for @liz: 1) routing rule is active (tenant->fallback) 2) spare attached and warm-mirroring validated 3) gradual rollout in progress (60% at 12:58) 4) ops quarantined bad nodes for RMA 5) customer informed and prefers in-region restore. Please finalize rollout to 100% when comfortable and send customer update.

liz - oncall-next: got it. I'll monitor next 30m, push to 100% when stable, and post the customer-facing note.

arnold - cs: thanks all. QuasarTech appreciates the speed. Requesting postmortem + RCA + timeline once available.

jamal - eng-sre: will own postmortem. Drafting timeline & logs now, will link ticket HWT-5902 and incident timeline.

sara - oncall: closing pager for oncall shift. Leaving channel open for ops updates. thanks team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert resolved for oncall-sara. Incident remains active for ops / postmortem tracking.
